Subject: Post-call: Embeddings model fit & validation plan for Acme Retail

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to validate embeddings for your semantic search POC:

What we heard
- Primary goal: improve product search relevance for long-tail SKUs and reduce false positives on similar descriptors.
- Dataset: ~100k product records, mix of short titles and longer descriptions; some legacy SKUs have OCR noise.
- Success signals: Precision@10 uplift, higher MRR on re-ranked results, and fewer manual corrections in CS flows.

Redwood recommendation (short):
- Start with our mid-size embedding: redwood-emb-1-large (1024d) for initial quality baseline.
- If latency/cost is a concern, run redwood-emb-1-small (768d) for A/B evals — typically similar semantic mapping but lower compute.
- For noisy OCR-heavy records we recommend an experiment with our noise-robust encoder (redwood-emb-noise-2026) and contrastive fine-tuning on 1k curated pairs.

Validation plan (what we propose we do together)
1) You share a 1,000-doc anonymized sample (titles + descriptions) we can index for the POC.
2) We run: embedding generation (two models), nearest-neighbor retrieval (cosine), and compute metrics: Precision@10, MRR, Recall@100, and pairwise triplet loss on labeled pairs.
3) Provide a notebook + dashboard with per-category drift scores (KNN stability) and dimensionality analysis (intrinsic dimensionality / eigenvalue spectrum).
4) If quality regression concerns appear, we’ll run a prompt/set evaluation and recommend quantization or reranking strategies.

Attachments: I attached a brief benchmark CSV and evaluation notes (embeddings-benchmarks-20261005.csv, eval-notes-POC-plan.pdf) and a validation notebook we’ll use.

Next steps / asks
- Please confirm you can share the 1k sample by EOD Wednesday (Oct 7).
- If Monday or Tuesday works better for a technical deep-dive, Marcus can walk through the notebook and distance-tuning heuristics.

Happy to adjust the plan — copying Marcus and Rishi for scheduling and technical detail.

Best,

Hi Alex — happy to jump in with technical detail. Short answers first, then a couple notes.

1) Footprint: approximate storage per 1k embeddings (float32)
- redwood-emb-1-large (1024d): 1k * 1024 * 4 bytes ~ 4.1 MB
- redwood-emb-1-small (768d): 1k * 768 * 4 bytes ~ 3.0 MB
If you quantize to 8-bit we’re looking ~1MB (768d)–1.25MB (1024d) with minimal quality loss in many search workloads.

2) Dimensionality tradeoff:
- In our internal benchmarks on product catalogs, 1024d models give ~2–4 point absolute lift in Precision@10 and MRR vs 768d on long-form descriptions (noisy text). For short clean titles the delta is often <1 point.
- Given your latency target (~40ms), starting with 768d in an A/B alongside 1024d for a small slice is a pragmatic approach. If you see drift on difficult SKUs, we’ll promote 1024d for those categories.

3) PII: remove or hash any customer identifiers, order numbers, and full email addresses. Product titles/descriptions are fine. If you must include order metadata, please mask numeric IDs. We’ll maintain any shared samples in a locked S3 bucket and delete after the POC unless you request retention.

Validation & drift checks we’ll run (high level):
- Semantic metrics: Precision@10, MRR, nDCG@10 for labeled queries.
- Embedding stability: average cosine similarity to category centroid over time; KL-divergence on neighborhood distributions.
- Intrinsic dimensionality: scree plot eigen-spectrum on covariance of embeddings — helps detect collapse or over-concentration.
- False-positive analysis: sample nearest neighbors with manual labels to identify where the model confuses attribute tokens.

Notebook & assets: here’s the Drive folder with the notebook and a short eval script: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-embeddings-acme (same link I cc’d above). The attached validation-notebook.ipynb includes scripts to compute all above metrics and a small evaluation harness.

If it helps, I can run a quick smoke test on 200 records first and share results in 24 hours.

Cheers,
